title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: pp. 94-95 prove a theorem in a 'tame' analysis-situs setting. There, M is a set of pieces or strata X, X° is an interior and ∂X a boundary, and ∥ is a 'disjointness' relation. Lemma 4 on p. 95 shows that the interiors X° of distinct, incomparable pieces are mutually ∥. On this page Grothendieck tries to abstract the rest of the argument into a purely formal statement.

Setting in modern terms:
- M is a set with a symmetric, irreflexive relation ∥. This is an 'orthogonality space' in the sense of Dacey and Foulis-Randall.
- For A ⊂ M, put A^⊥ = {x : x ∥ a for all a ∈ A}.
- The supports are the biorthogonally closed sets S = S^⊥⊥, and supp A = A^⊥⊥.
- Σ = Σ_{M,∥} is the set of supports. It is a complete lattice with Inf = ∩ and Sup = (∪)^⊥⊥.
- ∁S = S^⊥ is an order-reversing involution, thanks to the symmetry of ∥.
- Irreflexivity gives S ∩ S^⊥ = ∅ (the least element), and dually S ∨ S^⊥ = M (the greatest element).
- So Σ is a complete ortholattice, via the polarity/Galois-connection construction of Birkhoff.

The 'Lemma': let (A_i)_{i∈I} be nonempty, pairwise orthogonal subsets of M. In the application, I = F̃ and A_i = X_i°. Set S_J = Sup_{i∈J} supp A_i. The claim is that J ↦ S_J embeds the Boolean algebra 𝔓(I) into Σ as a sub-ortholattice Σ'. That is, it is injective, commutes with arbitrary Sup and Inf, and satisfies S_{A∖B} = S_A ∩ ∁S_B for B ⊂ A.

The next page proves injectivity and reduces Inf-commutation to Lemma 3: S ∥ S' ⇒ S' = (S ∨ S') ∩ ∁S. Grothendieck marks this 'Faux ?'. The margin of this page also carries 'Faux ?' beside the Lemma.

The point: Lemma 3 is a form of the orthomodular law. Pairwise-orthogonal elements generate a Boolean subalgebra exactly in orthomodular lattices. For an arbitrary orthogonality space the claim fails. In the intended topological setting it must come from extra axioms (the 'Ab D' property, etc.), not from the bare formalism.
errors:
As stated (for an arbitrary symmetric irreflexive relation), the Lemma is false.
- Every complete ortholattice L arises as some Σ_{M,∥}: take M = L∖{0} with x ∥ y iff x ≤ y'.
- Take L = the hexagon O6 = {0, a, b, a', b', 1} with a < b, so b' < a'.
- Then a ∥ b', yet (a ∨ b') ∧ a' = 1 ∧ a' = a' ≠ b'.
- So both S_{A∖B} = S_A ∩ ∁S_B and commutation with Inf fail for the family {a, b'}.
- Grothendieck's own 'Faux ?' is therefore justified.

The missing hypothesis is orthomodularity of Σ: a ≤ b ⇒ b = a ∨ (b ∧ a'). Under it, Lemma 3 holds. With c ⊥ a, c ≤ (a∨c) ∧ a' and ((a∨c) ∧ a') ∧ c' = 0 force equality. In a complete orthomodular lattice, a pairwise-orthogonal family generates a complete Boolean subalgebra.
Injectivity and Sup-commutation (proved on p. 97) are correct in general. Only the Inf/relative-complement part needs orthomodularity.

ideas.what: From a symmetric irreflexive relation on a set, build the lattice of biorthogonally closed 'supports' with complementation S ↦ S^⊥
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality space / complete ortholattice of ⊥-closed sets (polarity, Galois connection)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (Lattice Theory, 1940, polarities); Dacey (1968); Foulis-Randall orthogonality spaces (1970s)

ideas.what: A pairwise-orthogonal family of nonempty sets yields a Boolean-algebra embedding 𝔓(I) → Σ commuting with Sup and Inf
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonal family generates a Boolean subalgebra / block (true in orthomodular lattices, false in general ortholattices)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard orthomodular lattice theory (Foulis, Holland, Kalmbach)

ideas.what: Lemma 3 (next page): S ∥ S' ⇒ S' = (S∨S') ∩ ∁S, flagged 'Faux ?'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Husimi (1937), Birkhoff-von Neumann quantum logic tradition

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'support' formalism for tame topology/analysis situs is literally the orthogonality-space / quantum-logic construction. The point where his argument breaks is exactly orthomodularity. This suggests that the right axiom for his 'disjointness' relation on strata is one making Σ orthomodular (or Boolean). Neither he nor, apparently, later work on his analysis-situs notes names this link.
missed.quote: Soit M un ens muni d'une relation sym. antiréflexive ∥, d'où une notion de sous-support, support … et l'antiinvolution ∁ canonique … [marge: Faux ?]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Anyone reconstructing Grothendieck's 1986 analysis situs, e.g. o-minimal or 'tame' topology foundations, would know which lattice-theoretic axiom (orthomodularity) the strata relation must satisfy. Otherwise they risk repeating this false general lemma.

deep.surprise_reason: The formal content is the classical orthogonality-space → complete-ortholattice construction. The lemma is false in general, and Grothendieck himself suspected this. The only mildly interesting point is the implicit link to orthomodularity within his unpublished tame-topology program.
transcription_corrections: Margin reads 'Faux ?' (written vertically beside the Lemma), consistent with the 'Faux [?]' on p. 97.
'(en l'occurrence, I = F̃, A_i = X_i°)': the superscript is the interior symbol °, matching X° on p. 95, not 0.
'induit un isomorphisme de 𝔓(I) sur un sous-ensemble Σ' de Σ': the inserted Σ' names the image subset.
